requirements.evidence: All core requirements and the contract are implemented: `Queue::DEFAULT_PREFIX_MAP` and range fallback (app/Models/Queue.php:24,55), array cast (:38), save-time normalization/validation (:42-49,:89-130,:132-162), daily per-prefix `nextCode` (app/Models/Ticket.php:43-72), `issue_date` date cast (:162), single clock in issuance (app/Actions/IssueTicket.php:27,47-48,61-62), factory alignment/priority/day allocation (database/factories/TicketFactory.php:44-67), `priorityPrefixMap` param with atomic validation (app/Actions/UpdateQueue.php:21,27-38,73-74), column/backfill/index migration (database/migrations/2026_10_29_000001_add_issue_date_to_tickets_table.php:16-26) and docs. Two edge cases are imperfect: `down()` can fail on real daily-duplicate data (:43-44) and a 0-based key map is JSON-encoded as an array rather than an object.

conventions.evidence: Writes stay in domain actions (`UpdateQueue.php:21`, `IssueTicket.php`), the map is deliberately kept out of `#[Fillable(['entity_id', 'name', 'slug', 'is_active', 'labels_i18n'])]` (Queue.php:13), both migrations have reversible `down()` methods, public methods got PHPDoc (Queue.php:51-54,65-68,80-88; Ticket.php:29-42), tests are Pest feature tests matching siblings, and all required docs are synced (docs/business-rules.md, docs/database-schema.md, CHANGELOG.md).

security.evidence: Authorization is unchanged and runs before any validation/mutation (`Gate::forUser($actor)->authorize('update', $queue)`, UpdateQueue.php:23); the map is not mass-assignable (Queue.php:13, verified by TicketCodePrefixTest.php:50-57); every key and value is validated server-side (Queue.php:100,145-158, and effective-prefix uniqueness :117-127); no views, escaping, secrets or client-trusted parameters are involved. No weakness found.

tests.evidence: tests/Feature/TicketCodePrefixTest.php covers defaults/range fallback (:19), custom map + empty-to-null (:33), mass-assignment (:50), invalid keys/values/effective uniqueness (:58), per-prefix sequencing and daily restart (:72), legacy/malformed codes (:98), factory alignment (:108), explicit codes (:126), UpdateQueue update/atomic rejection (:139) and omission (:165); existing IssueTicketTest was updated to the N prefix. Gaps: the required `priority_prefix_map` error key is not asserted (:154,:161), no end-to-end issuance with a custom prefix, and the alignment test mixes a fixed date with real `now()` (:115).

simplicity.evidence: Mostly lean and reuses existing code (`Ticket::nextCode` plus one model hook instead of a service layer). Unnecessary flexibility remains: `nextCode()` accepts `int|string $priority` where a letter means a pre-resolved prefix but no caller uses that form (Ticket.php:45-55), it re-queries the queue (:52), and `whereDate` wraps the indexed date column (Ticket.php:62).

readability.evidence: Clear, focused helpers with accurate docblocks (Ticket.php:29-42,76-86; Queue.php:51-54,65-68,80-88,132-162), consistent naming and style with sibling files, no debug output or dead files; the normalization logic reads top-to-bottom and error messages are specific.

scope.evidence: The diff is limited to the feature: queue/ticket models, IssueTicket/UpdateQueue, TicketFactory, two new migrations, one new test file, and doc updates; the docs/api/totem.md example change is justified docs-freshness for the same behavior, and no UI, totem API code or unrelated refactors were added.

issues.explanation: `down()` re-adds `unique(['queue_id', 'code'])`, which fails once the new scheme has legitimately produced the same code on two different days, leaving a partially rolled-back schema; the rollback needs to deduplicate or drop the old-index restoration.

`normalizePriorityPrefixMap` returns a plain int-keyed array, so a valid map whose keys form 0..n-1 (e.g. `{"0": "X"}`) is JSON-encoded as `["X"]` instead of the documented JSON object; it still round-trips through the array cast, but the stored shape contradicts docs/database-schema.md.

The invalid-map `UpdateQueue` tests assert only `ValidationException`, not the contract-mandated `priority_prefix_map` error key, and no test asserts that a custom map actually changes the code emitted by `IssueTicket`.

The factory-alignment test creates one ticket on the fixed date 2026-09-28 and another at real `now()`, so its N001/N002 expectations invert if the suite runs on 2026-09-28; freezing the clock would make it deterministic.

`nextCode()` now accepts `int|string $priority` where a single letter is treated as an already-resolved prefix, but no caller uses the letter form; the dual meaning is speculative API surface that would be simpler as a separate resolved-prefix helper or an explicit prefix argument.

`whereDate('issue_date', $date)` wraps the column in `DATE(...)`, so the new `(queue_id, code, issue_date)` index cannot filter by day; `where('issue_date', $date)` is equivalent for a DATE column and index-friendly.

review.summary: The change implements priority-derived ticket prefixes with per-queue overrides, model-level validation and a daily per-prefix sequence, plus the schema migration, factory alignment, UpdateQueue support and docs. Requirements and conventions are covered thoroughly and the new Pest suite exercises most edge cases; the remaining points are nits such as a rollback hazard in the `issue_date` down migration, a JSON storage-shape edge case, missing assertions on the validation key/custom-prefix issuance, and a date-dependent test. Confidence is medium because the diff alone cannot confirm other callers/tests of the old `A` codes or the exact name of the pre-existing unique index.
